canonical.title: Wildcard Matching
canonical.sourceFilePath: 14. Dynamic Programming/5. DP on Strings/09. Wildcard Matching.cpp

narrative.title: The Access Log Filter
narrative.scenario: A security appliance matches access-log lines against admin-supplied filters. A filter may contain '?' standing for exactly one arbitrary character and '*' standing for any run of characters — including none. The whole line must satisfy the filter, not just a fragment. The matching engine decides, for every (line, filter) pair, whether the pattern covers the line end to end.
narrative.inputFormat: A string s (the log line) and a pattern p containing letters, '?', and '*'.
narrative.outputFormat: Return true when p matches the entirety of s under the wildcard rules, otherwise false.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
p contains lowercase English letters, '?', and '*'

testCases.explanation: A lone 'a' cannot cover two characters.
'*' absorbs the whole line, including the empty run.

hintLevels: Level 1: '?' consumes exactly one character; '*' is the fork — it either eats one more character or vanishes.
Level 2: match[i][j] = match[i-1][j-1] on literal/'?' match; on '*', match[i-1][j] or match[i][j-1].
Level 3: A pattern prefix made only of stars matches an empty string — seed that edge before filling.
